function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how you can create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has a GPU attached (the closest match to an “RTX A6000” that is currently offered by GCP is the `nvidia-tesla-a100`).  
The example uses the `gcloud` CLI because it is the simplest way to spin up a GPU instance and automatically handles authentication, quota checks, and driver installation.

---

## 1️⃣  Prerequisites

| Step | What you need | How to do it |
|------|---------------|--------------|
| 1 | **Google Cloud SDK** (`gcloud`) installed | `curl https://sdk.cloud.google.com | bash` (or follow the official install guide) |
| 2 | **Project ID** | `PROJECT_ID=$(gcloud config get-value project)` |
| 3 | **Billing enabled** on the project | `gcloud beta billing projects link $PROJECT_ID --billing-account YOUR_BILLING_ACCOUNT_ID` |
| 4 | **Compute Engine API enabled** | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| 5 | **GPU quota** for your region | Check via `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="region:(us-central1)"` and request more if needed |

> ⚠️ **Important:** GCP does not offer an exact “RTX A6000” GPU. The `nvidia-tesla-a100` is the closest high‑end GPU available in many regions. If you specifically need an RTX A6000, you would have to use a different provider (e.g., AWS with `p4d.24xlarge` or Azure with `NDv2`).

---

## 2️⃣  One‑liner `gcloud` command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create my-gpu-instance \
    --zone us-central1-b \
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 200GB \
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
        # Install NVIDIA driver
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y linux-headers-$(uname -r)
        sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
        # Reboot to load driver
        sudo reboot'
    --scopes cloud-platform \
    --tags gpu-instance \
    --description "Ubuntu 20.04 LTS with NVIDIA A100 GPU" \
    --labels env=dev,team=ml
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The Compute Engine zone where the instance will live. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & memory configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPU + 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Uses the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the public `ubuntu-os-cloud` project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk. |
| `--accelerator` | Attaches one `nvidia-tesla-a100` GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy TERMINATE` | If the host machine is reclaimed, the VM will terminate (useful for preemptible workloads). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Automatically restarts the VM if it crashes. |
| `--metadata startup-script` | Bash script that runs at first boot – installs the NVIDIA driver and reboots. |
| `--scopes cloud-platform` | Gives the instance full access to all Google Cloud APIs (needed for driver installation). |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules. |
| `--description` | Human‑readable description. |
| `--labels` | Key/value pairs for cost allocation and filtering. |

> 📌 **Tip:** If you prefer a *pre‑installed* driver image, you can use the `projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/ubuntu-2004-focal-nvidia-driver-535` image instead of installing manually.

---

## 3️⃣  REST API equivalent

If you want to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), here’s a minimal `curl` example:

```bash
PROJECT_ID=my-gcp-project
ZONE=us-central1-b
INSTANCE_NAME=my-gpu-instance
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/accelerators/nvidia-tesla-a100",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y linux-headers-\\$(uname -r)\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "labels": { "env": "dev", "team": "ml" },
  "description": "Ubuntu 20.04 LTS with NVIDIA A100 GPU"
}
EOF

curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> 🔑 **Authentication:** The example uses Application Default Credentials (`gcloud auth application-default login`). In production, you’d typically use a service account key file and set `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`.

---

## 4️⃣  Post‑creation steps

1. **Verify GPU visibility**  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute ssh my-gpu-instance --command "nvidia-smi"
   ```
   You should see the A100 listed.

2. **Install CUDA/CUDNN** (if you plan to run deep learning workloads)  
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-2 libcudnn8-dev
   ```

3. **Set up firewall rule** (if you need external access)  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-ssh-gpu \
       --allow tcp:22 \
       --target-tags gpu-instance \
       --description "Allow SSH to GPU instances"
   ```

---

## 5️⃣  Summary

| What | Command |
|------|---------|
| Create instance with GPU (CLI) | `gcloud compute instances create …` (see above) |
| Create instance with GPU (REST) | `curl -X POST …` (see above) |
| Verify GPU | `gcloud compute ssh … --command "nvidia-smi"` |
| Install CUDA | `sudo apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-2` |

Feel free to copy/paste the snippets into your terminal or CI scripts. Let me know if you’d like help automating this via Terraform, Deployment Manager, or a custom script!
